summary: Former Wise County, Virginia lookout whose glass cab on steel legs is described in 1950 and 1963 records; listed as gone.

facts.design: Glass-enclosed cabin on four steel legs, overall height about 50 feet (1963 survey description)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone. No source gives a removal date or describes what remains on the knob.

events.note: A tender kept groceries in the tower building; Wise County forest warden Owen C. Carter was directing fire fighting that year.
April 1950: warden Owen C. Carter had broken a leg while repairing a telephone line to the tower and had directed fire fighting from bed for two months (Kingsport News, April 26, 1950).
Tower building broken into; carbide and groceries taken. The December 1950 report calls it the second break-in.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the survey point on the cabin roof.

evidence.supports: Fire lookout tower in Wise County
Survey point at the apex of the roof of a glass-enclosed cabin on four steel legs; overall height about 50 feet
evidence.quote: THE POINT OF INTERSECTION WAS THE APEX OF THE ROOF OF THE GLASS ENCLOSED CABIN THAT IS MOUNTED ON FOUR STEEL LEGS. THE OVERALL HEIGHT IS ABOUT 50 FEET.

evidence.supports: Station about 6 miles northwest of Wise and 5.5 miles southwest of Pound
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS LOCATED ABOUT 6 MILES NORTHWEST OF WISE AND 5-1/2 MILES SOUTHWEST OF POUND.

evidence.supports: Tender kept groceries in the tower building in 1950
evidence.quote: some groceries which had been stored there by the tender

evidence.supports: Tower building broken into a few nights before the December 1950 report
evidence.quote: the Buck Knob tower building was broken into a few nights ago by unknown parties
who carried off several cans of carbide and some groceries
This is the second time this tower has been entered.

evidence.supports: Warden Owen C. Carter, Wise County forest warden
evidence.quote: Owen C. Carter, Wise County forest warden

evidence.supports: Carter broke a leg repairing a telephone line to the tower and directed fire fighting from bed for two months
evidence.quote: has been directing fire fighting and fire prevention for the past two months flat on his back from a broken leg, sustained while repairing a telephone line to the Buck Knob Lookout Tower.

evidence.supports: Latest dated item on the page is the 1963 survey description
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1963 (ELH)

evidence.supports: TopoZone map page still lists a Buck Knob Lookout point in Wise County
evidence.quote: Buck Knob Lookout is listed in the Towers Category for Wise County in the state of Virginia.

evidence.supports: 1963 directions ran through a pipe gate
evidence.quote: TO A PIPE GATE, PASS THROUGH AND GO 2.45 MILES TO THE END OF ROAD

sources.title: Buck Knob Lookout topo map, Wise County

notes_for_editor: The 1950 newspaper items and the 1963 survey description are solid; the status is from the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. No build date, height to the cab floor, agency or removal date was found, so none is stated. The 50 ft figure is an overall height from the survey, not height to the cab floor, so it is not in height_m. Newspaper credits on the Forest Lookouts page are Kingsport News (April 26, 1950) and Middlesboro Daily News (December 11, 1950). Access and ownership are unknown; do not treat the site as visitable without a current source.
